text:
Dylan Holloway is doing most of what made his first St. Louis season work, and the goals have not come. He has four on 6.57 expected, shooting 8.3%, and one goal in his last ten games despite games of seven shots against Detroit and five apiece against Montreal and the Rangers. That is the kind of slump our numbers call due: the chances are there, the finish is not.

The rest of his game holds up. The Blues get 53.81% of expected goals at 5v5 with him on and are 6.25 points better than without him. He skates fast (94th percentile top speed), shoots hard, and has 45 hits, which makes him one of the more physical scoring forwards around.

The cold stretch has hurt in a specific way: our wins-added ranks him 509th of 530, because the chances he did not convert came at moments that mattered. Evolving-Hockey had him 20th among forwards in wins above replacement last season, while warning that some of that came from hot shooting. This season is the other side of that coin. If his shooting drifts toward his normal range, the points follow.
headline: Dylan Holloway keeps getting the looks
